Formula of the submodel of a project() run

Source: R/methods.R
formula.projection.Rd

For a projection object (returned by project()), this method gives the formula of the submodel of the projection. The formula has the form that projpred uses for the submodel fits. Use it, for example, to set up the submodel in another package. For a list of projection objects, use lapply().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'projection'
formula(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class projection (returned by project()).

...

Currently ignored.

Value

A formula.

Details

The right-hand side has an intercept and the predictor terms of x (see predictor_terms()), with two changes that projpred applies to its submodel fits:

  • The group-level terms of one grouping factor are merged into one term. For example, (1 | g) + (x1 | g) becomes (x1 | g).

  • A linear main-effect term is dropped if the submodel also has a smooth term of the same variable. For example, x1 + s(x1) becomes s(x1).

The term labels of the formula can differ from predictor_terms() in the order of the variables of an interaction (for example, x2:x1 instead of x1:x2).

The left-hand side is the response of the formula of the reference model object (element formula of the output of get_refmodel()). It has only the response variable, so it can differ from the left-hand side of the reference model fit:

  • For a two-column binomial response (cbind(successes, failures)), the left-hand side is only the first column. The projection still uses the numbers of trials (successes + failures): projpred keeps them in the reference model object (element wobs), not in the formula.

  • For a brms reference model, the left-hand side is only the response variable, without addition terms such as trials() or weights(). The projection still uses them: projpred keeps the numbers of trials (or the weights) in the reference model object (element wobs), not in the formula.

  • For the latent projection, the left-hand side is the latent response.

Observation weights and offsets are not part of the formula. projpred fits the submodels with the offsets of the reference model (as an argument of the submodel fitter) and adds the offsets to the predictions. If you fit the submodel in another package, add the offsets there.

The environment of the formula is that of the reference model formula.

With refit_prj = FALSE in project(), the submodel fits come from the search. After an L1 search, these fits are the L1-penalized fits of the search path. A fit of this formula in another package gives other coefficients.

Examples

# Data:
dat_gauss <- data.frame(y = df_gaussian$y, df_gaussian$x)

# The `stanreg` fit which will be used as the reference model (with small
# values for `chains` and `iter`, but only for technical reasons in this
# example; this is not recommended in general):
fit <- rstanarm::stan_glm(
  y ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5, family = gaussian(), data = dat_gauss,
  QR = TRUE, chains = 2, iter = 500, refresh = 0, seed = 9876
)

# Projection onto an arbitrary combination of predictor terms (with a small
# value for `nclusters`, but only for the sake of speed in this example;
# this is not recommended in general):
prj <- project(fit, predictor_terms = c("X1", "X3", "X5"), nclusters = 10,
               seed = 9182)
print(formula(prj)) # gives `y ~ X1 + X3 + X5`
#> y ~ X1 + X3 + X5
#> <environment: 0x5b5d5e972680>
